 CAT's Sales Volumes Rise Across Segments: Can Growth Continue?
 3 min read CAT Caterpillar Inc. CAT is seeing a broad-based recovery in equipment demand, with higher sales volumes driving revenue growth across its major businesses. After a prolonged period of volume weakness, the construction and mining equipment manufacturer returned to volume growth in the second quarter of 2025. Since then, improving end-user demand and favorable dealer inventory movements have supported an increasingly strong recovery. The momentum has continued through the first nine months of 2026, prompting the company to maintain its expectation of mid-to-high-teens revenue growth for the full year. 
 In the third quarter of 2026, higher sales volumes contributed $2.2 billion to Caterpillar's revenues, accounting for 13.2% of the year-over-year revenue increase and taking total sales and revenues to $20.68 billion. Volume growth had contributed 17.3% and 19.9% to revenue growth in the first and second quarters, respectively. Overall, higher volumes added $7.64 billion to revenues during the first nine months of 2026. 
 Construction Industries has been the biggest contributor, adding $4.1 billion to revenues during the first nine months of 2026. The improvement primarily reflected higher equipment sales to end users, indicating strengthening underlying demand. 
 Power & Energy contributed approximately $2.5 billion in volume growth over the same period. Strong demand for large reciprocating engines, turbines and related services, particularly for data centers, supported performance. Oil & Gas also benefited from higher demand for reciprocating engines used in gas compression applications and aftermarket parts. Increased sales of turbines and turbine-related services provided further support. 
 Resource Industries added $1.2 billion to revenues through higher sales volumes in the first nine months of 2026. The improvement primarily reflected increased equipment sales. In Mining, Heavy Construction and Quarry & Aggregates, sales benefited from the impact of changes in dealer inventories. Higher rail services sales also contributed to growth. 
 Looking ahead, Caterpillar's major businesses appear well-positioned to benefit from favorable industry trends. Construction Industries should gain from continued infrastructure spending, increased heavy construction activity and rising investments in data center development. 
 Resource Industries is expected to benefit from favorable commodity prices, demand for mining fleet replacements and improving activity in Heavy Construction and Quarry & Aggregates. 
 Meanwhile, Power & Energy is likely to remain an important growth driver, supported by rising demand for reciprocating engines, turbines and related services. The expansion of data centers to support cloud computing and generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasing the need for reliable power solutions. Additionally, growing prime power requirements are supporting demand for turbines, turbine-related services and reciprocating engine products. 
 How Are CAT's Peers Performing? 
 Komatsu KMTUY reported a 5% revenue increase to $7 billion in the quarter ended Sept. 30, 2026. Construction, Mining & Utility Equipment sales rose 15%, while Industrial Machinery & Others sales decreased 2.9%. For fiscal 2027 (ending March 31, 2027), Komatsu expects net sales to grow 7.7%, with gains of 8.2% in Construction, Mining & Utility Equipment and 7.9% in Industrial Machinery & Others. 
 Terex Corporation TEX reported a 58.4% year-over-year sales increase to $2.2 billion in the third quarter of 2026. Pro forma net sales grew 11.6% year over year, driven by growth in Materials Processing, Specialty Vehicles and Aerials. 
 Supported by its backlog and business momentum, Terex expects approximately 8.5% pro forma sales growth in 2026, with revenues projected between $8 billion and $8.2 billion. By segment, Terex expects sales to grow low double digits in Materials Processing and Aerials, high single digits in Specialty Vehicles and Environmental Solutions to remain flat compared with their respective prior-year baselines. 
 CAT’s Price Performance, Valuation & Estimates 
 CAT shares have gained 8.7% over the past year compared with the industry’s 1.5% growth. 
 Caterpillar is currently trading at a forward 12-month price/earnings (P/E) ratio of 18.72X compared with the industry average of 17.45X. 
 The Zacks Consensus Estimate for CAT’s 2026 earnings indicates year-over-year growth of 43.4%. The consensus mark for revenues implies an increase of 17.3% for the year. The earnings estimate for 2027 indicates around 19.8% growth, with revenues rising 11%. 
 Earnings estimates for Caterpillar for both 2026 and 2027 have moved down over the past 60 days.
